analysis.evidence: וַיֵּרֶד יַהְוֶה לִרְאֹת means “and Yahweh came down to see.” The infinitive לִרְאֹת gives the purpose of his descent, to see the city and the tower.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ forms a Qal wayyiqtol with the third-person masculine singular verb. Its subject is יַהְוֶה.
Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: YHWH came down to look at the city and the tower. The repeated object marker אֶת identifies both structures as the objects of לִרְאֹת.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לִ־ introduces a Qal infinitive construct expressing the purpose of the descent.
Direct-object particle with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add Genesis 11:5 to the verse evidence for the existing city sense of עִיר in article 3yr.
draft.definition: A built settlement, a city or town.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:5 calls the settlement הָעִיר, “the city,” as it takes up the builders’ proposal for עִיר וּמִגְדָּל, “a city and a tower,” in Genesis 11:4.

analysis.evidence: In אֶת הָעִיר וְאֶת הַמִּגְדָּל, the repeated object marker pairs the city with the tower. אֲשֶׁר בָּנוּ, “which they built,” identifies both as the works Yahweh came down to see.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes עִיר, a feminine singular common noun in the absolute state. The article has qamats before ע.

draft.change: Add Gen.11.5 as an example of the existing definite-object sense at word index 0.
draft.definition: Introduces the definite person or thing that a verb takes as its direct object.
draft.evidence: Gen.11.5 repeats אֶת before הַמִּגְדָּל, the second object of לִרְאֹת.

analysis.evidence: In לִרְאֹת אֶת הָעִיר וְאֶת הַמִּגְדָּל, “to see the city and the tower,” each definite noun has its own object marker. The conjunction on the second marker joins the tower to the city as a second object of seeing.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וְ means “and.” The unsuffixed particle אֶת marks the following noun phrase as a direct object.
analysis.sense: Marks the tower as the second definite direct object of לִרְאֹת, “to see.”

analysis.evidence: וְאֶת הַמִּגְדָּל marks the tower as the second object of לִרְאֹת, alongside the city. The clause אֲשֶׁר בָּנוּ identifies them as structures the people built.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ doubles the initial מ of the common noun. The noun is singular and absolute, and its gender is unmarked here.
Indeclinable relative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In אֲשֶׁר בָּנוּ בְּנֵי הָאָדָם, the people are the builders, and the preceding nouns הָעִיר and הַמִּגְדָּל identify what they had built: the city and the tower.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural. The ending וּ agrees with the plural subject בְּנֵי הָאָדָם.

draft.change: Add Genesis 11:5 as a plural example of the existing ben-member sense.
draft.definition: In construct, בֵּן can identify someone as a member of the group named by its complement. The plural בְּנֵי הָאָדָם means human beings.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:5 names בְּנֵי הָאָדָם as the people who built the city and tower.

analysis.evidence: In אֲשֶׁר בָּנוּ בְּנֵי הָאָדָם, “which human beings built,” בְּנֵי הָאָדָם is the subject of the plural verb בָּנוּ. The phrase identifies the builders of the city and tower as human beings.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural construct of the common noun בֵּן. The ending ־ֵי marks the plural construct before הָאָדָם. The initial ב belongs to the noun.
analysis.sense: Members of the group named by the following noun, here humankind.

analysis.evidence: בְּנֵי הָאָדָם means “the sons of humankind” and identifies the people who built the city and tower. The plural verb בָּנוּ refers to those builders, while הָאָדָם denotes humanity collectively.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הָ precedes a masculine singular absolute noun. The noun completes the construct phrase בְּנֵי הָאָדָם.
